top.title: Beyond Nvidia: Why AI giants like OpenAI, Google and Amazon are building custom chips
top.snippet: The AI race is heating up as tech giants like OpenAI, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft design their own chips to optimize AI operations. This strategic move aims to cut soaring deployment costs and gain control over crucial infrastructure, moving beyond just building better models. While Nvidia's GPUs still lead in training, custom silicon is emerging as a vital asset for companies navigating the accelerating AI landscape.
top.aiSummary: OpenAI, Google, Amazon and Microsoft are designing custom AI chips to reduce deployment costs and control infrastructure, challenging Nvidia’s dominance in training hardware.

editorialTake:
AI is becoming a closed club, even as commerce platforms open their doors wider. The clearest signal comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, who are now restricting access to their latest models, GPT-5.6 Sol and Mythos 5, to customers vetted by the Trump administration during a cybersecurity review. At the same time, these AI giants, alongside Google and Amazon, are pouring billions into custom chip design and infrastructure, Amazon alone just committed $13 billion to AI infrastructure in India. The message is clear: control the hardware, control the access, and you control the future of AI.

Contrast this with the retail tech world, where Google is slashing Play Store fees and letting developers use their own payment systems, while Flipkart and Amazon race to build out quick-commerce fulfillment in India. The barriers to entry for merchants are dropping. Shopify reports that shoppers arriving via AI-powered platforms like ChatGPT are 50% more likely to buy than those from organic search. Yet, the very AI engines driving this growth are becoming less accessible to outsiders, as the biggest players lock down their most powerful tools and infrastructure.

Some will argue that democratization is still happening at the application layer, and that open-source models or new entrants will keep AI accessible. That holds only if the cost and performance gap between proprietary and open models does not widen further. With custom chips and government-aligned access controls, the gap is set to grow.

Luxury and jewellery leaders should not assume that AI-powered commerce will remain a level playing field. The next quarter is the time to audit dependencies: which AI tools, APIs, or platforms are mission-critical, and who really controls them? Start building direct relationships with AI providers, and invest in teams that can adapt quickly if access tightens. The brands that move now will be the ones with leverage when the doors start to close.
oneSentenceSummary: Even as Google and Amazon lower barriers and decentralize platforms, the largest AI players are consolidating ecosystem power through hardware, access controls, and selective partnerships.
